text: With the template written and parameterized, deploying it is one command: az deployment group create, pointing at the Bicep file and supplying every parameter value. The password comes from an environment variable set immediately before the command runs — never typed in plain text, never committed to source control.

Deploying prod is the exact same command with different values: a different resource group, different server and database names, and a different secret variable for the password. The template file and its resource definitions never change between the two — that's Lesson 5's parameterization paying off directly.

A deployment command returning success is one signal, but it's worth checking a second, independent one: the Azure Portal's own deployment history for that resource group. Checking two separate systems, rather than trusting a single source of truth, is the same habit a DBA uses after any production change.

Overlook now has a real, reproducible Azure SQL environment — but no firewall rule yet, no auditing, and no failover group. Chapter 3 builds the security and compliance layer on top of this foundation, starting with encryption.
